safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the absence of unwell contacts has limited impact in this presentation because management is primarily guided by the patient’s own symptoms and exam findings; it is mainly contextual/epidemiologic information. This omission is unlikely to change immediate clinical decisions or safety.

Delayed review in deterioration scenarios can meaningfully worsen outcomes even if the current working diagnosis is viral illness.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold ('no fevers'). Transcript supports hot/cold/sweats but does not clearly document 'subjective fevers' as a stated fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Recording “subjective fevers” when the gold standard indicates no fevers could bias clinicians toward higher suspicion of bacterial infection and increase unnecessary antibiotics, testing, or mis-triage. In this case the transcript describes hot/cold sweats, so the overstatement is plausible but still may lead to mild overtreatment rather than missed critical care.
